title: Migrate TLS private key loading to secretx URIs
description: Why: TLS key paths in TlsConfig across transit, reader, mail, and smtp are bare filesystem paths. Accepting secretx: URIs would allow TLS private keys to be stored in AWS Secrets Manager or other backends, which is useful for automated certificate rotation. What to do: Change key_path fields in each TlsConfig to accept either a bare path or a secretx: URI. At TLS setup time, if the value is a secretx: URI, resolve it via secretx::from_uri().get().await and pass the resulting bytes to rustls's load_private_key_from_memory(). Bare paths continue to use the existing file-read path. Note: PKCS#11 for TLS is typically handled at the TLS library level and is out of scope here — this only covers secret retrieval, not offloading TLS signing to an HSM.
notes: Part of epic stoa-6c0f1855 (Integrate crate-secretsx). Blocked on stoa-f0b9ff15 (workspace wiring). Lower priority (P3) — only needed if secrets-manager-sourced TLS keys are a goal.
